name: Myo-reps / drop sets

lead: Drop sets and myo-reps are intensity techniques that pack more hard repetitions into less time so you get more muscle-building work per minute. A drop set keeps going with a lighter weight after failure at a heavier one; myo-reps use one high-effort set followed by several short mini-sets with brief rests.

Both keep the muscle working near failure for more total reps in a short window, which advocates say raises the growth stimulus per minute. Drop sets have a long history: Henry Atkins described the multi-poundage system in the late 1940s and they were part of Joe Weider's system in the 1980s. Coverage says drop sets may increase muscle growth more than traditional three-set training, while some researchers report mixed findings; a 2026 trial compared myo-reps with straight sets in resistance-trained men.

paras: Lifters tack them on to the last set of an exercise or use them for isolation moves when time is short. They are used inside a normal split alongside heavier compound work.
Working to failure adds fatigue and soreness, and general resistance-training injury risks apply. No technique-specific harm data were identified.

chain: Extra hard reps in less time
angle.text: Lifters use drop sets and myo-reps to pack more hard reps into less time, so shorter workouts still give a strong growth stimulus. Drop sets go back to the 1940s and may add growth compared with traditional sets, with some mixed findings. Myo-reps were only recently compared with straight sets in a trial.

lead: Drop sets and myo-reps are resistance-training intensity techniques meant to pack more hard repetitions into less time. A drop set continues exercising with a lighter weight after reaching muscle failure at a heavier one [1]. Myo-reps are a related method in which a lifter performs an initial high-effort set and then several short mini-sets with brief rests; a 2026 trial compared the approach with traditional straight sets in resistance-trained men [2].

Drop sets have a longer documented history: Henry Atkins, editor of Body Culture magazine, described the approach in the late 1940s as the multi-poundage system, and drop sets were part of Joe Weider's Weider System in the 1980s [1]. Encyclopedic coverage says drop sets may increase muscle growth more than traditional three-set training, while some researchers report mixed or inconclusive findings [1].
infobox: Described late 1940s by Henry Atkins as the multi-poundage system [1]
More work near failure in less time

paras: Drop sets are most often done on weight machines but can also use dumbbells and other free weights [1]. Myo-reps pair a heavy-effort activation set with brief-rest mini-sets, and are promoted as a time-efficient alternative to several straight sets [2].

An encyclopedic summary reports that, in adults in their 50s, 12 weeks of thrice-weekly drop-set training improved muscle mass, strength, endurance and functional tasks, and that other researchers have reported mixed or inconclusive results [1].

A study published in the Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research in 2026 examined session duration, muscle excitation and barbell velocity for a myo-reps protocol versus a traditional protocol in resistance-trained men, alongside a training comparison [2]. A registered trial also compares myo-reps with traditional sets for strength, fat-free mass and time efficiency [3]. Results beyond those described in the study titles are not summarised here.
These techniques appear in general muscle-building advice shared in physique communities. No forum material specific to the entry was identified.

Human studies exist but are few. A 2026 trial compares myo-reps with straight sets in resistance-trained men [2], a registered 2025 trial examines strength, fat-free mass and time efficiency [3], and drop-set training has been studied in older adults [1].

lore.intro: Lifters discuss myo-reps and drop sets as ways to save time while still training hard.

claims.claim: Myo-reps give the same muscle growth as straight sets in less time.
Drop sets build more muscle than conventional sets.
